$ xref deps

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options
  3. Examples
  4. A Rust release built with cargo-auditable
  5. One crate, as JSON
  6. A Go binary

  10. Provenance

List what a binary says about how it was built: the dependency manifest Rust's cargo-auditable embeds in .dep-v0, or the module list Go embeds in .go.buildinfo, together with the compiler and linker strings from .comment and the GNU Build-ID (or Mach-O LC_UUID). Use it to see which crates or modules a stripped release contains, at which versions, before reading any code.

Usage

xref deps [OPTIONS]

Arguments and options

Options

--filter <FILTER>
Case-insensitive substring filter on package or module name.
--json
Emit structured JSON output instead of human-readable text.

Examples

A Rust release built with cargo-auditable

uv (Astral's Python package manager) ships its release binaries with the dependency manifest embedded. The root package, then every runtime and build dependency with its version:

Command
$ xref -b uv deps
Output

A Go binary

The GitHub CLI gh is a static Go binary without unwind tables; deps reads its .go.buildinfo module list anyway:

Output

A binary without a manifest

The official ripgrep release is not built with cargo-auditable (and has no Build-ID note); deps prints its toolchains and says that there is no manifest:

Command
$ xref -b rg deps
Output
toolchain GCC: (GNU) 9.4.0 | rustc version 1.83.0-nightly (adf8d168a 2024-09-08) | GCC: (GNU) 9.2.0
no embedded dependency manifest (.dep-v0 or .go.buildinfo)
stderr
xref: load 2.8ms, total 8.8ms

Reading the output

  • build-id is the GNU Build-ID note (ELF) or LC_UUID (Mach-O) in hex.
  • toolchain lists the distinct .comment strings: compilers and linkers of the binary and of the objects linked into it, so a Rust binary often names a C compiler too.
  • ecosystem rust (.dep-v0) rows are name version kind, where kind is runtime or build and [root] marks the package the binary was built from. ecosystem go (go1.x) names the Go toolchain and the main module; its rows are module version module. With --json each Go module also has its h1: checksum in source and, when the module was replaced, the replacement in replaced_by.
  • The same data is in xref query '{"operation":"dependencies"}' and in the triage of info (see query and mcp).

Limits

  • Only what the binary embeds: a Rust binary built without cargo-auditable has no manifest, and the crates it contains are not guessed from strings.
  • The .dep-v0 stream is decompressed to at most 16 MiB from at most 4 MiB; a larger or corrupt section is reported, not parsed.
  • Without a .go.buildinfo section header the Go header is searched in the load segments, only at 16-byte aligned addresses and at most 64 times.
  • Versions are the strings the build recorded; nothing is checked against a registry or an advisory database.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.5.0 (the remapped release build of commit b00d4a14, made by scripts/package-release.sh before the tag) on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release); uv = uv 0.13.7 (official x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release, built with cargo-auditable); gh = GitHub CLI 2.103.3 (official linux_amd64 release, a static Go binary). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
